Part A — Predict the Output.


Question #1

What is the output of each line? Explain briefly with your own words.

```{r}

m <- matrix(1:6, nrow = 2)
apply(m, 1, sum)

```

a. apply(m, 1, sum)

  apply(m, 1, sum) — I got 9 and 12. Since the 1 stands for rows, I think it just adds across each row of m.
  
```{r}

m <- matrix(1:6, nrow = 2)

apply(m, 2, sum)

```

b. apply(m, 2, sum)

  I got 3, 7, and 11. Here the 2 means columns, so to me it adds down each column instead.

```{r}

m <- matrix(1:6, nrow = 2)

class(lapply(1:3, function(i) i^2))

```

c. class(lapply(1:3, function(i) i^2)) 

  This gave "list". Even though it squares 1, 2, and 3, I noticed lapply() always hands back a list, so its class is "list".

```{r}

m <- matrix(1:6, nrow = 2)

sapply(1:3, function(i) i^2)

```

d. sapply(1:3, function(i) i^2)
  
  This gave 1, 4, and 9. To me, sapply() makes things simpler and turns the squared numbers into a normal vector.

```{r}

m <- matrix(1:6, nrow = 2)

sapply(c('a', 'bb', 'ccc'), nchar)

```



```{r}

m <- matrix(1:6, nrow = 2)

mapply(function(x, y) x * y, 1:3, 4:6)

```



```{r}

m <- matrix(1:6, nrow = 2)

tapply(c(10, 20, 30, 40), c('u', 'v', 'u', 'v'), sum)

```
